questions.enonce_markdown:
**SECTION A - DIRECTED WRITING (30 marks)**

Mark distribution: Content (14 marks); Expression and Accuracy (12 marks); Slanting (04 marks).

You are the secretary of the School Life Association of GHS Aboh. A crisis meeting about social media was held and some parents were of the opinion that social media was destroying their children while others thought it was a necessary evil. Selecting relevant information from the notes below, develop the minutes of the meeting, stating the benefits and dangers of the social media. Paying attention to grammar, spelling, punctuation and handwriting, write in TWO paragraphs of not more than **150 words**.

**Notes**

- Meeting at GBHS Aboh - 10:30am
- Social media has grown tremendously in the last year.
- Facebook and twitter have grown much faster and have captured millions of users in just a few years
- Since anyone can create a fake account and do anything without being traced, it has become quite easy for anyone to bully on the internet. Threats, intimidation, messages and rumours can be sent to the masses to create discomfort and chaos in the society.
- People from anywhere can connect with anyone and old friends discovered.
- Personal data and privacy can be hacked and shared in the internet.
- It glamorizes drugs and alcohol. People start to follow others who are wealthy or drug addicted and share their views and videos which may inspire others to follow and get addicted to drugs and alcohol
- It is very easy to learn from other experts who are professionals.
- Addicts spend time that could have been utilized for more productive tasks and activities.
- Fraud and scams are frequent
- Security agencies have access to personal accounts which makes privacy almost compromised
- You can update yourself on the latest happenings around the world
- Promotes business to the largest audience
- Held on the 7th March 2018
- For donations to the needy and Non-Governmental Organisations.
- Most people have used social media platform to propose and marry one another, after sometime, they realize they were wrong in their decisions and part ways.
- Government agencies fight crime. They use this platform to spy and catch criminals
- Creating a story and spreading on social media can easily ruin someone's reputation
- So much time spent on social media can lead to weight gain and excessive use of networking sites can bring disorder in routine life.
- However, these are advantages and disadvantages to decide which way to go about social media.
- Many children have died trying to copy what they see others doing on social media
- Very useful to those in the city
- People from different communities can connect to discuss and share related issues thereby building communities.
- You can share your issue with the community to get help.
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Model answer (two paragraphs, 143 words)**

The crisis meeting on social media was held at GBHS Aboh on 7th March 2018 at 10:30am. Members agreed that social media has grown tremendously and is dangerous. Fake accounts make bullying, threats and false rumours easy, and personal data and privacy can be hacked and shared. It also glamorizes drugs and alcohol, so some children copy what they see and have even died. Addicts waste productive time, fraud and scams are frequent, and too much use leads to weight gain.

However, members also noted real benefits. People can reconnect with old friends, learn from professional experts, share issues in communities and update themselves on world events. Businesses reach large audiences, donations reach the needy, and government agencies use it to catch criminals. Since it has both advantages and disadvantages, it was resolved that parents should guide their children in using it wisely.

**Why this works (selection and slanting).** The task asks for the minutes of a meeting that state BOTH the benefits and the dangers of social media. The first paragraph therefore opens with the facts of the meeting (the crisis meeting, GBHS Aboh, 7th March 2018, 10:30am) and keeps only dangers (fake accounts and bullying, rumours and threats, hacked personal data and privacy, glamorizing of drugs and alcohol, children dying while copying what they see, time wasted by addicts, fraud and scams, weight gain). The second paragraph keeps only benefits (reconnecting with old friends, learning from experts, building communities, updating oneself on world events, promoting business, donations to the needy, helping security agencies catch criminals) and ends with the decision of the meeting. The notes that do not serve this purpose are left out (the growth of Facebook and twitter, marriages that end in separation, "very useful to those in the city"). The language is the formal, impersonal style of minutes (past tense, reported decisions: "Members agreed...", "it was resolved that..."), written in the candidate's own words, in exactly TWO paragraphs of fewer than 150 words.

**Marking guide**

| Criterion | Marks | What earns the marks |
|---|---|---|
| Content | 14 | Relevant points chosen from the notes: the details of the meeting, several dangers and several benefits of social media; no irrelevant or contradictory notes |
| Expression and Accuracy | 12 | Own words (no lifting of whole notes), varied linking, correct grammar, spelling and punctuation, TWO paragraphs, 150 words at most |
| Slanting | 4 | The text reads as the minutes of the meeting, in a formal style, and balances the dangers and the benefits as the question requires |

**Common mistakes**

1. Copying the notes one after the other, in the order given, instead of selecting and grouping them.
2. Writing a letter or an essay instead of the minutes of a meeting, or forgetting the details of the meeting (place, time, date).
3. Giving only the dangers or only the benefits, or writing one paragraph or three paragraphs instead of TWO, or going over 150 words.
